items.title: Pentagon surges a third carrier and 10,000+ troops toward the Mideast
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt sailed from San Diego for the Middle East, giving the US the potential for three carrier strike groups in the region (first time since the 2003 Iraq invasion); the USS Makin Island group (2,200 Marines) also deployed, with USS Boxer already near Hormuz. Axios separately reported two extra Patriot batteries positioned in Saudi Arabia and Qatar to protect oil/gas facilities.
items.source_name: Bloomberg via gcaptain; Axios via ANI

items.title: Tanker attacks in Hormuz hit their highest weekly level since the war began
items.summary: Reuters reported at least 12 attacks, attempted attacks, or harassment incidents hit oil, LNG, and LPG tankers around Hormuz in the week of Sep 28 - Oct 5 — the most in any week since the war began Feb 28. The US Navy-led JMIC said Iran's actions show 'intent to assert presence along key transit lanes.'

items.title: Atlantic: White House asked Pentagon for pre-midterm Iran strike options
items.summary: The Atlantic reported (citing two administration officials) that the White House directed the Pentagon to develop limited Iran strike options usable before the Nov 3 midterms, with bigger post-election options also under discussion. Axios separately reported CENTCOM was told to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat. Advocates reportedly conceded limited strikes would not reopen Hormuz or lower gas prices pre-election.

items.title: IRGC adviser: Iran will 'soon' close 'unauthorized routes' in Hormuz
items.summary: IRGC commander adviser Mohammad-Reza Naqdi said Iran's armed forces fully control the strait, that it stays closed until Iran's 'legitimate' demands are met, and that 'passages created by violators through the explosion or destruction of some rocky routes... will soon be closed.' He added Iran's weapon ranges are capped only by policy decisions and can be extended whenever authorized.
items.source_name: UNB via TBS News; ScanX News

items.title: Hegseth visits USS Lincoln, releases Iran-war combat stats
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew to the USS Abraham Lincoln, presented a Presidential Unit Citation from Trump, and disclosed the strike group's Iran-war tally: 64 Iranian warships sunk, 21 anti-ship cruise missiles destroyed, 3,693 combat sorties, 450 Tomahawk launches, 1.37M lbs of ordnance. The Navy confirmed 8 suicide attempts (no deaths) across the group during a 264-day stretch without a port call.

items.title: USS Lincoln returns to San Diego after record 321-day deployment
items.summary: USS Abraham Lincoln docked at San Diego after 321 days deployed, including 264-265 uninterrupted days at sea (a modern Navy record), spent supporting the Iran war after starting in the Indo-Pacific. It is the second record-length carrier return of the war (USS Gerald R. Ford returned in May after 326 days).

items.title: Trump rules out striking Iran before the Nov 3 midterms
items.summary: In a Truth Social post, Trump said the US 'will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,' while claiming oil is flowing in record volumes through Hormuz (22M bbl 'last night alone') and that the blockade remains 'in full force and effect.' He said talks with Iran were 'productive.' Analysts noted his Hormuz flow claim is disputed.

items.title: Iran's nuclear chief: enrichment 'indispensable,' won't be surrendered
items.summary: AEOI head Mohammad Eslami called uranium enrichment 'an indispensable part' of the nuclear process and dismissed renewed US demands — VP Vance had said Iran must make 'meaningful' enrichment reductions as a war precondition — as 'a mere bunch of lies aimed at deception.' On Oct 11 he added Iran will not give up nuclear technology under foreign pressure. AEOI spokesman Kamalvandi said Iran would secure its interests 'through diplomacy or on the battlefield.'

items.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on 17 vessels moving Iranian crude
items.summary: The US imposed new sanctions on individuals, networks, and 17 vessels transporting Iranian crude, oil products, and petrochemicals — continuing economic pressure alongside the naval blockade, even as Trump paused strikes.

items.title: UKMTO: outbound tanker struck by projectile inside Hormuz
items.summary: UKMTO reported that the master of an outbound tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit on the port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire; crew safe. The same day, masters near Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) reported being ordered off anchorages via VHF broadcast. Authorities are investigating.
items.source_name: UKMTO via DefconLevel; Eagle Intel maritime desk

items.title: IRGC Navy claims three tankers struck naval mines on 'unauthorized routes'
items.summary: The IRGC Navy said three crude supertankers struck naval mines while attempting to exit Hormuz via unauthorized routes with navigation systems switched off — one each on Oct 10, Oct 11, and Oct 12 morning, all engulfed in flames. It warned any vessel cooperating with US forces or switching off AIS would be treated as 'hostile' and face a 'decisive response.' Vessel names and nationalities were not independently confirmed.
items.source_name: IRGC Navy via PressTV/Tasnim; Anadolu Ajansi

items.title: MT Petro Dolphin drone attack at Sohar (Oman): 2 Indian seafarers missing
items.summary: MT Petro Dolphin was hit by a drone at Sohar anchorage, Oman; of 11 Indian crew, 9 were rescued and 2 remain missing. India's MEA condemned the attacks; the Indian embassy in Muscat is coordinating with Omani authorities. Separately, MT Valthera (Marshall Islands-flagged) was struck by an unknown projectile near Hormuz, caught fire, with its 11 Indian crew reported safe.

items.title: Iran calls US response to its seven Hormuz conditions 'inadequate'
items.summary: Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said the US had accepted some of Iran's seven conditions for reopening Hormuz and returning to talks, but the response was 'inadequate' — the strait stays closed to the US until all are met. Iran had presented the proposal at the UNGA (reopen within seven days if conditions met); the US replied via Qatari intermediaries.

items.title: Tehran reviewing US reply; Qatar and Pakistan mediating; FM rejects US 'open strait' claim
items.summary: FM spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran is still reviewing the US response and will reply via intermediaries; Qatar and Pakistan are among the mediators. He rejected Trump's normalcy claim: 'security would not return to the Strait of Hormuz as long as the United States continues its naval blockade and economic war against Iran.' Reuters noted the core impasse: Washington wants Iran's nuclear program addressed from the outset; Tehran wants Hormuz reopening and security first.

items.title: Brent hits ~$105-106.65; Goldman raises Dec Brent forecast to $90
items.summary: Brent crude rose to ~$105-106.65/bbl on Oct 12 (WTI ~$92.5-93.7) on the tanker-attack wave and Riyadh airport strikes — up >70% this year. Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast $5 to $90/bbl, estimating >$20/bbl of current price is geopolitical/supply-disruption risk premium.

The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker MT Valthera, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 11, triggering an onboard fire; all 11 crew are reported safe. India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned both Sunday attacks (Valthera and the Petro Dolphin drone strike) and demanded immediate de-escalation through dialogue.
items.title: MT Valthera hit by projectile in Hormuz on Oct 11; India condemns Sunday tanker attacks

items.summary: US Central Command said a US fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged cargo vessel M/V Ocean Molica (also known as Arika Sun) in the Gulf of Oman on Oct 10 after it ignored repeated warnings and tried to run the US naval blockade; the strike fully disabled its propulsion with no crew injuries. CENTCOM tally since the blockade resumed July 14: four commercial vessels disabled, 135 turned around, 10 IRGC-linked tankers destroyed.
items.title: US fighter jet disables M/V Ocean Molica (Arika Sun) in Gulf of Oman for running Iran blockade

items.event_time_ist: Oct 11, 2026 (reported; aired on Iranian state TV over the weekend)
items.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran finds the latest US response to its Hormuz conditions 'insufficient' and is 'no longer responding' to Washington, telling IRNA the US must clarify its position (it accepted some of the seven conditions, others unclear). He warned that undersea communications cables, data centers and AI facilities in the region - US-linked assets he put at over $2 trillion - would be targeted if intense fighting resumes: previously held-back targets 'will be within firing range.'
items.title: Iran's Rezaei threatens undersea cables, data centers, AI facilities if war resumes; calls US reply 'insufficient'

items.source_name: OilPrice (citing Argus and Iranian state media)
items.summary: The IRGC Navy warned that any ship inside the Strait of Hormuz that switches off its navigation and identification systems will be 'identified as hostile and dealt with severely and decisively' (Iranian state media). The IRGC also claimed a third supertanker struck naval mines on an 'unauthorized route' since Saturday - the vessel was not identified and the claim could not be independently verified. CENTCOM has previously denied IRGC mine-strike claims.
items.title: IRGC Navy warns 'dark-mode' ships in Hormuz will be treated as hostile; claims third mine strike (unverified)

items.summary: Mohsen Rezaei held a phone conversation with India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval on Oct 12, exchanging views on regional and international developments and bilateral ties, per the Iranian Embassy in India. The call comes as New Delhi presses for Indian-seafarer safety after the Oct 11 attacks and two missing crew from the Petro Dolphin.
items.title: Iran's Rezaei speaks with India's NSA Ajit Doval amid Gulf shipping attacks

items.summary: Reuters reported vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen to their lowest in more than two months after tanker attacks reached their highest weekly level since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February; Brent held above $103/bbl.
items.title: Hormuz tanker traffic at lowest in 2+ months as attacks peak - Reuters

items.summary: At his Monday press conference, Iranian FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei confirmed Tehran is still reviewing the US response to its proposal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and that message exchanges with Washington continue through Pakistan and Qatar, whom he called the principal mediators. He said Iran's preconditions, including its seven conditions, must be respected, rejected claims that Tehran's Hormuz posture is negotiation leverage, and said Iran is open to helping resolve the Saudi-Houthi crisis through dialogue.
items.title: Baghaei: Iran still reviewing US Hormuz response; Pakistan, Qatar still mediating

items.summary: Speaking at the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned pressure across the energy chain will intensify until the Strait of Hormuz fully reopens and confidence returns, flagging diesel near $200/bbl and commercial onshore inventories below 6 billion barrels. Aramco is studying additional crude-export routes and expanding overseas storage. Top BP, ExxonMobil, Shell and TotalEnergies executives skipped the event after the Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport. Kpler put Hormuz flows at 10.5M bpd for the week through Oct 10, ~38% below prewar levels.
items.title: Aramco CEO: energy supply pressure to intensify until Hormuz fully reopens

items.summary: Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast to $90/bbl from $85, estimating geopolitical tension adds just over $20/bbl to current prices and saying its base case does not assume a quick US-Iran resolution. The bank warned Brent could average ~$125 next year if Gulf output stays 5M bpd below prewar levels. Brent traded ~$106.65 on Oct 12, up 1.8%, as Houthi attacks on Riyadh and doubts over the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire outweighed Russian diesel supply news.
items.title: Goldman raises December Brent forecast to $90 on lingering Iran-war supply risks

items.summary: UKMTO said Monday that three vessels — a container ship, a product tanker and a crude oil tanker — were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, Oct 11. Two appear to match the already-known Oct 11 incidents (MT Petro Dolphin drone attack off Sohar; MT Valthera projectile strike in the strait); the container ship is a third vessel type not previously reported. UKMTO did not name the vessels or give casualty details.
items.title: UKMTO: three vessels — container ship, product tanker, crude tanker — struck by unknown projectiles in Hormuz on Oct 11

items.summary: UKMTO received a time-late report (Warning 168-26) on Monday that a products tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while conducting an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 12. Authorities are investigating; UKMTO did not name the vessel or report casualties. This extends the Hormuz strike run to at least four distinct incidents across Oct 11–12.
items.title: UKMTO Warning 168-26: products tanker struck by unknown projectile outbound through Hormuz, Oct 12

items.summary: The IRGC Navy (via IRNA) now describes the third vessel in its Oct 10–12 mine-claim series as a shuttle tanker carrying 750,000 barrels of crude, hit on an "unauthorized route" Sunday Oct 12 with an explosion and severe fire. This conflicts with earlier IRGC-linked coverage that described the same claimed incident as a 2-million-barrel supertanker; the vessel remains unidentified and the claim unverified.
items.title: IRGC says third 'mine-strike' vessel was a 750,000-barrel shuttle tanker

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (trading session; Monday settle Oct 12 was $106.65)
items.summary: Brent fell roughly 1% to about $105-$106/bbl on Tuesday and WTI to about $92-$93, pulling back after Monday's $106.65 close (highest since Sep 15). Traders weighed possible additional Russian diesel supplies against Gulf supply risks; ANZ said further downside is limited by escalating tensions. Fresh Kpler data showed confirmed Hormuz flows crashed to just 2M bpd on Saturday (vs 6.7M Friday, 22.8M Thursday), with the seven-day average at 10.5M bpd, ~38% below the prewar 17.1M bpd baseline. Separately, OPEC+ ministers said Monday that shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels - over a third of the value of the commodities being moved.
items.title: Oil pulls back Tuesday: Brent ~$105-$106 as Russian diesel hopes meet Gulf supply risk; Hormuz flows collapsed to 2M bpd Saturday (Kpler)

items.summary: Citi Research's base case (60% probability) assumes Hormuz flows recover in Q4 with no lasting infrastructure damage: Brent falls to $70/bbl in Q1 2027 and toward $65 from Q2 2027. But it assigns a 30% probability to prolonged disruption or further infrastructure damage, which would keep Brent averaging $120 through 2027. The bank says the timing of any normalization remains unusually uncertain.
items.title: Citi: Brent could slide to $65 in 2027 if Hormuz normalizes (60% base case), or average $120 if disruption persists (30% case)

items.event_time_ist: Oct 9, 2026 (time of attack unknown); confirmed by India’s shipping minister on Oct 10, 2026
items.title: MT GEM NO. 2 hit by drone at Sharjah Anchorage, Oct 9 — all 22 Indian crew safe
items.summary: The Panama-flagged crude tanker MT GEM NO. 2 was struck by a drone while at anchorage off Sharjah (UAE) on Oct 9, 2026. India’s Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed the incident and said all 22 Indian crew members are completely safe; his ministry is monitoring the situation and in contact with the ship manager. No perpetrator has been named. The incident marks a drone attack deep inside UAE coastal waters at the mouth of the Gulf of Oman — a notable geographic escalation beyond the strait’s transit corridors. This Oct 9 attack predates the Oct 11 Petro Dolphin/Valthera incidents but was missed by earlier checks; it is now in the timeline.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026, late afternoon IST (gaggle before Youngstown, Ohio rally)
items.title: Trump: midterms won't sway Iran strategy; war 'will end very soon'; Houthis 'misbehaving very badly'
items.summary: Speaking to reporters Monday before his Youngstown, Ohio rally, Trump said the Nov 3 midterms will not influence US strategy toward Iran and repeated that the war 'will end very soon' (with oil prices to 'drop like a rock'). He confirmed he spoke directly with Saudi Crown Prince MBS about Houthi airport attacks; asked about a US response to the Houthis, he said only they are 'misbehaving very badly' and announced no retaliatory measures.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026, ~7:50 AM IST (Youngstown, Ohio rally, evening Oct 12 ET)
items.title: Trump says US 'might have gone too far' targeting Iran's leadership; claims all 159 Iranian naval vessels sunk
items.summary: At the Youngstown, Ohio campaign rally, Trump said the US may have 'gone too far' in targeting Iran's leadership — 'we don't know who the hell we're dealing with any more' — complicating negotiations. He also reiterated the claim that Iran has lost its air force and all 159 naval vessels, now 'resting beautifully in the bottom of the sea'.
items.source_name: The Business Standard (TBS) / Rifnote (via Al Jazeera)

items.summary: Israel's Channel 14 (Oct 11) and The Jewish Edition (Oct 12) report the IRGC ran a large-scale missile/drone exercise on Sunday, Oct 11 — described as one of its largest military demonstrations since the Feb 28 US-Israeli offensive. Drills included Emad and Kheibar ballistic missiles, waves of Shahed-136 kamikaze drones, air-defense tests, and IRIAF fighter-jet activity over Tehran and other cities; the IRGC-linked Saberin News channel published launch footage. Caveats: some circulating videos appear recycled, and claims of hypersonic missile launches are unverified. The demonstration follows an Oct 9 Bloomberg report citing Western officials who warn Iran has preserved its missile/drone manufacturing capacity and that Russia may be supplying missiles to help Tehran rebuild its arsenal — an assessment the White House disputes.
items.title: IRGC launches 30+ ballistic missiles and Shahed-136 drone waves in its largest exercise since the war began

items.summary: JFeed reported Monday afternoon (Oct 12) on initial, limited-details reports of a ballistic missile launched from Yazd, Iran. It is unclear whether this is a distinct launch or part of the IRGC's large missile/drone exercise on Oct 11; no second outlet has confirmed a separate Yazd launch.
items.title: Initial reports of a ballistic missile launch from Yazd, Iran

items.event_time_ist: Oct 11, 2026 (individual incident times unknown; warnings issued Oct 11-12)
items.summary: UKMTO warnings 164-26 through 169-26 now document SIX commercial vessels struck on Sunday, Oct 11 — five tankers (an outbound tanker, an outbound crude tanker, an outbound product tanker, plus the MT Petro Dolphin UAV strike near Sohar anchorage, Oman) and one inbound container ship — the highest single-day total since the war began. Four of the reports were time-late, meaning official incident counts had been undercounting the wave. The warning-164 tanker suffered steering-gear-room and port-water-tank damage and proceeded to Fujairah; the Sohar tanker was first classified as suspicious activity before UKMTO upgraded it to a UAV attack, with local authorities evacuating the crew. Splash247 adds UKMTO has now logged at least 18 reported attacks region-wide this month. This materially upgrades the three-vessel Oct 11 count reported overnight.
items.title: UKMTO: six vessels struck Oct 11 (five tankers + a container ship) — highest single-day total of the war

items.summary: On Oct 9 the Pentagon corrected its Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS): the official US death toll for operations against Iran rose from 18 to 21 after adding two noncombat deaths — Army National Guard Maj. Sorffly Davius, 46, who died in Kuwait on March 6, and an unidentified Navy service member who died by suicide in September — while 865 service members are now listed as wounded. A third death, Sgt. Devin A. Seibel, 26, killed in a May training accident in Iraq, was logged under Operation Inherent Resolve (not Iran-connected), bringing total US military deaths in the Middle East since Feb 28 to 22. The correction follows the Washington Post's September report that DCAS was undercounting deaths, which Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had called "fake" and "a complete lie"; House Armed Services Democrats Adam Smith and Chrissy Houlahan said there is "no excuse for a mistake of this magnitude."
items.title: Pentagon raises official Iran-war death toll to 21, admits prior undercount

items.summary: A War Department official told DefenseScoop on Oct 9 that the Pentagon will introduce a new "Pending Adjudication" category in DCAS to track casualties awaiting final categorization and will standardize hostile and non-hostile casualty subcategories, changes triggered by an "internal audit of our reporting systems." In a statement to Military.com on Oct 12, the Pentagon said the tweaks are meant to make casualty data "more easily understood." The overhaul follows months of scrutiny over Iran-war casualty counts, which the Pentagon had reconfigured mid-conflict after Trump declared Operation Epic Fury over in May despite ongoing fighting.
items.title: Pentagon overhauls casualty reporting: new 'pending adjudication' category for DCAS

items.event_time_ist: Evening of Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 (newly reported Oct 12-13)
items.summary: The IRGC Navy issued repeated 'serious warning' broadcasts on marine Channel 16 ordering vessels at anchor in Oman's Khasab harbor (Musandam peninsula), Mina Saqr, and Ras al Khaimah (UAE) to weigh anchor and 'go back to Dubai anchorage'. Ambrey said six commercial ships anchored ~16.5 nm off Ras al Khaimah were told Saturday evening to leave immediately; UKMTO logged the incident as 'suspicious activity' (security notice 161-26) without identifying the sender. Omani authorities normally jam IRGC transmissions aimed at vessels in Omani waters, but this one got through; some ships complied and headed west. Separately, Iran declared a prohibited area covering all of Oman's territorial waters off the Musandam peninsula (map first aired on Al Jazeera Arabic) — assessed as a response to the US 'Project Freedom' escort posture. A particular threat to Oman, whose Musandam fishing communities have no road access and depend on resupply by ship.
items.title: IRGC Navy ordered anchored ships in Omani and Emirati waters to relocate via VHF, widening its maritime control zone

items.event_time_ist: Press release Oct 13, 2026, ~5:30 AM IST; underlying letter sent Oct 8, 2026
items.summary: Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO), with Reps. Ansari and Jacobs, wrote to SecDef Hegseth demanding answers on the Sept 1, 2026 strike at a wedding in Kuhestak, Iran, which killed 5 civilians (incl. a 4-year-old and a 16-year-old) and injured dozens. WaPo reporting cited 'high likelihood' the U.S. was responsible; the letter also presses on the Minab school strike (175 killed Feb 28) and the Lamerd sports-hall strike (21 killed), plus the gutting of Pentagon civilian-harm mitigation staff (CENTCOM CHMR down to 1 full-timer). Answers demanded by Oct 26. A separate eir.news report notes 74 members sent a related letter on Oct 8.
items.title: House members press Pentagon on Sept 1 Kuhestak wedding strike that killed 5 civilians

items.event_time_ist: announced ~8:05 PM IST, Oct 13 (incident time unknown)
items.title: Iran's Army Navy claims a 'violating' oil tanker caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The Iranian Army Navy (Nedaja) announced Tuesday morning via state news agency IRNA that an oil tanker described as 'violating' caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz. No details were given on the nature of the violation, the vessel's identity, damage extent, or crew casualties. This is a separate claim from the IRGC Navy's Oct 10-12 mine-strike claims: it comes from the regular Army Navy and places the incident east of the strait (i.e., in the Gulf of Oman approach), which would extend Iran's claimed enforcement zone beyond the strait if it reflects a new event. Tasnim published boat-shot footage of a burning tanker alongside the claim. No independent confirmation; treat as an Iranian-state claim.

UKMTO reported Tuesday (17:30 UTC) that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile off Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; local authorities reported a fire aboard that has since been extinguished, with all crew safe and no environmental impact reported. Regional outlets (Al Arabiya English, Iran International, Gulf News) carried the breaking UKMTO alert; Iran International/Gulf News graphics suggest a second vessel (a container ship) may also have been hit — details still developing. Comes as Iran and Oman discuss a temporary joint shipping corridor.
items.title: New UKMTO warning: tanker struck by unknown projectile in Hormuz on Tuesday — fire out, crew safe

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (statement to Parliament; joint statement released same day)
items.summary: UK PM Andy Burnham told Parliament Monday that the Sept 27 suspected drone/explosives plot at RAF Fairford — the base US bombers used for Iran strikes — was 'highly likely coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by the IRGC'; Britain sanctioned two IRGC-linked men (counterespionage chief Ruhollah Bazghandi and facilitator Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki). The US State Department released a joint statement the same day with 28 allied governments recognizing the UK's attribution and condemning Iran's covert operations in Europe. Iran rejects any connection (Ambassador Seyed Ali Mousavi via IRNA).
items.title: UK blames IRGC for RAF Fairford plot; 29 nations back the attribution

items.summary: Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said Monday that Iran and its allies wrongly assessed Gulf Arab countries were 'the weakest link' in the US-Israel war against Iran, posting that 'we are all targeted and that our security is indivisible' and urging joint Gulf action to defend against attacks by Iran and its proxies.
items.title: UAE's Gargash calls for 'joint Gulf action' against Iran and its proxies

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 (tanker ~11:00 PM IST / 17:30 UTC; container ship time undisclosed)
items.summary: UKMTO said on Tuesday that a container ship AND a tanker were struck by unknown projectiles within the Strait of Hormuz, with authorities investigating and no further details yet. This upgrades the 12:55 PM PDT alert, which had only the off-Khasab tanker (17:30 UTC, fire extinguished, crew safe) as UKMTO-confirmed and the container ship as merely 'suggested' by regional graphics. Two commercial vessels hit in one day inside the strait.
items.title: UKMTO confirms a container ship AND a tanker struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday

items.event_time_ist: Wednesday, Oct 7, 2026 (~7:00 PM UTC Oct 7 / ~12:30 AM IST Oct 8; UKMTO Warning 158-26)
items.summary: A chemical/oil tanker was struck by multiple projectiles ~1900 UTC Oct 7 about 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar — UKMTO Warning 158-26, with casualties reported (numbers/severity undisclosed; authorities investigating). The vessel was later identified as the Acers, an Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical and oil tanker. This was the first tanker attack deep inside the Persian Gulf in nearly a month (since a Sep 9 strike southeast of Al-Faw, Iraq), a major escalation of the threat's geography: most October attacks have been in or near Hormuz, but this one landed ~500 km west of the strait. UKMTO did not attribute the attack. WSJ: Brent jumped ~5% past $105 on Thursday as traders feared the surge spreading beyond Hormuz and complicating US-backed shuttle-run shipping arrangements. Catch-up: this incident was missed by earlier checks and is back-filled here with the correct event date.
items.title: Chemical/oil tanker Acers struck by multiple projectiles off Qatar, Oct 7 — first deep-Gulf attack in nearly a month, casualties reported (missed by earlier checks; back-filled)

items.event_time_ist: late Tuesday night, Oct 13 local Saudi time (early hours of Oct 14 IST)
items.summary: A Houthi ballistic missile hit Saudi Aramco's executive headquarters office complex in Dhahran late Tuesday; a company source told Reuters an office tower's top three floors were damaged and caught fire (blaze later put out), while the Saudi energy ministry confirmed only a limited fire and no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted the missile over Dhahran, with fragments falling on a residential area, and also destroyed three cruise missiles and two drones aimed at Riyadh and the south — debris wounded four people in Riyadh and damaged 15 homes. Hours earlier the coalition struck the Houthi-run Yemen Petroleum Company's Sabah fuel depot in Sanaa (Houthis: two civilians killed, two injured) after urging evacuations; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree had threatened a 'harsh and painful' response naming the Aramco HQ as a target. Brent climbed toward $106 on the Saudi supply risk (+0.8% to $106.58 by 0030 GMT Oct 14, WTI $94.94).
items.title: Houthi missile hits Aramco's Dhahran HQ complex; Saudi strikes Sanaa fuel depot in retaliatory exchange

items.event_time_ist: strategy adopted ~10 days ago (early Oct 2026); disclosed Oct 14
items.summary: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters that about ten days ago Tehran adopted new tactics — a change in the type and pace of attacks on ships it deems in violation of its Hormuz restrictions — with an explicit aim to keep global oil prices high and influence the Nov 3 US midterm elections: 'The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices.' The officials said the decision was taken at the highest levels, that Iran will expand operations beyond Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman and farther afield, and warned 'it will be complete closure soon.' A US military official corroborated one tactic shift: after the US destroyed much of Iran's radar, the IRGC began using unarmed spotters in small boats and dhows to identify targets including US naval vessels; last week US forces confronted one such dhow, ordered its crew off, and destroyed it (no casualties). Maritime security sources count at least five Hormuz-area incidents in the past 48 hours, and the US Navy-led JMIC kept its threat level at 'severe.'
items.title: Iran shifted Hormuz attack tactics ~10 days ago to keep oil high and sway US midterms, officials tell Reuters

items.summary: The US blockade has kept Iranian seaborne crude exports at zero through all of October, per energy-intelligence firm Vortexa — exports fell to zero in the second week of September from ~230,000 bpd and stayed there; 43 million barrels of Iranian crude sit trapped west of the Strait of Hormuz, with 83 million barrels total on the water. Iran's LPG exports fell 48% month-on-month, lowest since at least January 2023. Vortexa's Claire Jungman: the blockade 'is doing what years of sanctions never managed.' Russia now makes up 80% of 'high-risk exports' (Iran, Russia, Venezuela), whose combined 4.73M bpd in September was down from 6.39M a year earlier.
items.title: US blockade kept Iranian crude exports at zero all of October — Vortexa, Oct 13

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (exact hour of statements not published)
items.summary: IRGC Navy Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei told Iranian state TV his forces were 'waiting' for US warships to approach the strait's entrance to sink them, claimed a US carrier retreated 700 km, and said Iran exercises 'smart control' by issuing transit permits. CENTCOM dismissed it in an X post: the IRGC navy commander 'has no navy,' the strait is controlled by US forces and regional partners, which helped move over 19 million barrels of crude through the waterway on Monday. Exchange came alongside UKMTO reports of Tuesday's tanker + container-ship strikes in the strait (already in feed).
items.title: CENTCOM rejects Azmaei's claim of Iranian control over Hormuz; says commander 'has no navy'

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (exact hour of call not published)
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband spoke by phone Oct 13 (State Dept readout via spokesman Tommy Pigott), reiterating a shared commitment to safeguarding transit in the Strait of Hormuz and 'holding Iran to account for its actions.' They also discussed stabilizing global energy markets, a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war, and securing US assets in Britain. No new sanctions, naval deployments, or operational arrangements were announced.
items.title: Rubio, Miliband discuss Hormuz security in call; pledge Iran accountability, no new measures announced

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (ISW assessment posted on X; AP roundup published Oct 13, 2:16 PM EDT)
items.source_name: AP (via TTNews) / Institute for the Study of War
items.summary: The Institute for the Study of War said Oct 13 that Iran appears to be targeting commercial vessels conducting ship-to-ship oil transfers in and near the Strait of Hormuz in order to undermine energy movement through the strait — a deliberate tactic to reinforce Iranian control of the waterway and deter vessels from using non-Iranian-approved routes. ISW also said Iran may be developing its anti-ship missile capabilities. The assessment fits SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei's Oct 10 state-TV claim that Iranian forces are striking an average of five 'smuggling ships' a night — referring to the US effort to escort smaller shipments through the strait before transferring oil to larger tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman.
items.title: ISW: Iran now deliberately targeting ship-to-ship oil transfers in and near Hormuz

items.summary: The Houthi-controlled Foreign Ministry warned international airlines on Oct 13 that flights to Saudi airports are 'unsafe' except those serving Mecca and Medina, and military spokesman Yahya Saree declared Saudi Aramco oil facilities 'legitimate targets', telling employees and civilians to evacuate Aramco sites in Dhahran and Riyadh plus Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport — a sharp aviation-energy escalation after Tuesday's Saudi strikes on Sanaa. The US State Department raised its Saudi travel advisory to Level 3 ('Reconsider Travel', Level 4 for Yemen border areas); Etihad said it would cancel flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until Oct 19, with several other carriers (Lufthansa, Air France-KLM, Delta, Qatar Airways) suspending services. Context: follows Saturday's Houthi missile attack on King Khalid International Airport (Saudi aviation authority: at least 12 dead, 309 wounded; airport shut since) and Tuesday's Houthi missile hit on Aramco's Dhahran HQ complex (already alerted).
items.title: Houthis tell airlines Saudi airports are 'unsafe', order evacuations near Aramco sites; US raises Saudi travel advisory to Level 3
MI5 chief: Iran now targeting UK military sites; RAF Fairford plot 'not unique'
items.summary: MI5 Director General Ken McCallum said in his annual threat speech Tuesday that Tehran is seeking to hit military sites in Britain — a 'major shift this year' beyond its usual targets (dissidents, media, Jewish sites hit by proxies). He said the suspected September plot against the U.S.-run RAF Fairford air base is 'not unique,' with other examples 'not just in the U.K. but around the world.' McCallum said Iran's proxy attempts in Britain are low-level for now but warned Iran's IRGC has shown stronger capabilities closer to home. Separately, Iran summoned British Ambassador Hugo Shorter, warning it could 'seriously reconsider' bilateral relations unless the U.K. provides evidence linking Tehran to the Fairford plot. Seven men in their 20s were arrested and released on bail; 50+ arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year. The U.S. pulled its bombers from Fairford after the incident.

items.event_time_ist: Evening of Oct 13, 2026 local time (Wasilla, Alaska; overnight Tuesday, published 04:24 UTC Oct 14)
items.summary: At a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska (campaigning for Sen. Dan Sullivan), Trump declared: "Wait and see what we do to Iran. We're going to hit them hard... because we're pretty much fed up." He called Iran "a failed state" with 300% inflation that "doesn't pay its soldiers," said a decision on Iran comes "very soon," claimed Iran's nuclear facilities are buried under "thousands of tons of rock" and that Tehran was two weeks from a bomb. A sharp rhetorical break from his Oct 8 "no strikes before the midterms" line.
items.title: Trump threatens Iran at Alaska rally: "We're going to hit them hard"

items.event_time_ist: Reported Oct 13, 2026 (conversations took place last week)
items.summary: Axios (Barak Ravid, 4 sources: 2 US officials, 1 Israeli official, 1 with knowledge) reported Trump and Netanyahu discussed last week a major new operation against Iran before Israel's Oct 27 election and the US Nov 3 midterms. Netanyahu cited worrying Iranian nuclear rebuild steps (incl. possible Pickaxe Mountain enrichment site); Trump told him to "go ahead and get ready" but made no commitment. IDF and CENTCOM are on alert finalizing preparations (heavy bombing of energy infrastructure + nuclear targets); Hegseth and CENTCOM leaders are the strongest advocates, most Trump advisers prefer economic pressure. IDF chief Zamir told Joint Chiefs Chairman Caine renewed fighting within three weeks could force postponing Israel's Oct 27 election. White House official called the report "false" (reiterating no pre-midterm strikes); Israeli PMO denied Netanyahu pressured Trump.
items.title: Axios: Trump and Netanyahu discussed renewed Iran operation before elections

items.summary: Trump accused Yemen's Houthi militants of deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms, warning 'I'll be there after the elections, and I will never forget!' their attacks on Saudi Arabia. He told reporters he 'might' ask Turkish President Erdogan to intervene in support of Saudi interests ('President Erdogan, I think, would do as I ask'). Erdogan separately called Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Tuesday to condemn the Houthi attacks and pledge Turkey will stand by Saudi Arabia, as Ankara's Saudi-Pakistan defense pact heads to parliament.
items.title: Trump warns Houthis he'll 'never forget' Saudi attacks, floats Erdogan intervention

items.summary: Brent rose toward $107 a barrel on Wednesday (+0.8% to ~$106.5, WTI ~$95) after two more vessels were struck in Hormuz and Iran confirmed new anti-ship tactics aimed at keeping prices high into the midterms. Morgan Stanley raised its Dated Brent forecast by $5/bbl for this quarter and next, saying 'uncertainty around crude exports remains elevated' with Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure compounding the Hormuz disruption.
items.title: Brent toward $107 as Morgan Stanley raises Dated Brent forecast $5 on Hormuz/Houthi supply risk

items.summary: WSJ reports Iran is fortifying its defenses as it braces for potential renewed US strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. Satellite imagery analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security shows dirt mounds and passive barriers built around the Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear sites to obstruct ground raids; Tehran has used the fighting pause since late July to rebuild missile and drone production. The regime is also rallying the public (billboards advertising shoulder-fired-missile training, IRGC units visiting kindergartens) and has warned regional officials of wider escalation — including possible ground incursions into neighboring countries, strikes on US warships and Saudi oil facilities — if Washington resumes strikes. On the US side, a third carrier strike group and a Marine expeditionary unit are heading to the region while the Pentagon weighs more air defenses for regional bases.
items.title: WSJ: Iran fortifying nuclear sites and rallying public for potential post-midterm US strikes

items.event_time_ist: Oct 14, 2026, Wednesday morning local time (exact time unknown)
items.summary: Three fishermen were injured when a fishing boat was struck in an incident involving an unidentified drone near Sirik in southern Iran's Hormozgan province on Wednesday, the provincial governor's office said, as reported by Reuters and carried by Tasnim news agency. Tasnim cited local sources as describing it as an attack by a US drone, but Iranian authorities have not officially confirmed the circumstances or who was responsible. It is the first reported US-linked drone strike on an Iranian vessel in the area since the Sept 14 Kargan drone-boat clash.
items.title: Three fishermen injured in drone incident off Sirik, southern Iran

items.summary: Saudi authorities issued a mobile alert warning of a possible aerial threat in Riyadh and the Al-Kharj governorate on Wednesday amid the sharp Houthi-Saudi escalation, then sent a second message saying the danger had passed, according to Reuters and Arab News. No strikes in the capital were confirmed. The alert came hours after the Houthi missile hit on Aramco's Dhahran headquarters complex (already alerted) and Saudi coalition interceptions around Riyadh and the south.
items.title: Saudi Arabia issues then lifts aerial-threat alert for Riyadh
IRGC Navy claims container ship sank after striking mine south of Hormuz
items.summary: Iranian state media on Wednesday (Oct 14) shared an IRGC Navy statement saying a container ship carrying 2,500+ containers sank south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine while on what the Guards called an 'unauthorised and dangerous route'; the statement warned local vessels and fishermen to take care. No vessel identity, flag, crew status, or independent/UKMTO confirmation; first IRGC mine claim against a container ship (Oct 10-12 claims were tankers). Iranian-state-only, so unconfirmed.

items.event_time_ist: Letter dated Oct 9, 2026; first reported Oct 13, 2026
items.summary: Iran's ambassador/permanent representative to the IMO filed a formal protest letter dated Oct 9, 2026 (filed end of last week) accusing US military forces of repeatedly occupying VHF Channel 16 in the Persian Gulf for prolonged periods, addressing Iranian seafarers in Persian with 'threatening, abusive and provocative' language, and in some cases urging crews to abandon their vessels. Iran says this disrupts the protected distress/safety channel (citing IMO Res. A.954(23) and SOLAS) and asked the IMO to circulate the letter as an official document to all member states. TradeWinds notes Iran offered no transcripts; US had not responded at publication. Maritime Executive adds IMO's conflict tally: 106 incidents, 24 fatalities since Feb 28, with 15 attacks in October.
items.title: Iran lodges formal IMO protest accusing US forces of misusing VHF Channel 16 to intimidate seafarers

items.summary: Maritime security sources told Reuters Oct 14 that the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride (2,824 TEU) has SUNK after a projectile strike; Pakistan's Hydrographer issued an Oct 14 navigational warning noting the sunken vessel and floating containers. It is the second vessel lost since the war began Feb 28, per IMO data; Singapore's MPA confirmed all 21 crew were safely evacuated. The same sources report the Antigua & Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao — struck Sep 23 — is also sinking after a failed rescue attempt, per Vanguard. This upgrades this morning's unconfirmed IRGC mine claim (alerted 09:40Z): the IRGC claimed the ship hit a mine on an 'unauthorised route,' but independent sources attribute the loss to a projectile strike.
items.title: GFS Pride confirmed sunk near Hormuz — second vessel lost since war began; Cape Dao also sinking

items.summary: Tuesday Oct 13 saw FOUR ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz — not the two previously reported. AFP reports a British maritime agency logged two more vessels struck Tuesday by unknown projectiles with minor damage. SeaTrade Maritime (Vanguard Tech IDs): UKMTO issued four new warnings for Oct 13 covering container ships GFS Pride, GFS Giselle and Al Saadiyat plus tanker Alfonso. GFS Giselle took minor damage but continued, all 22 crew safe (MPA confirmed); Al Saadiyat suffered no significant damage or casualties on an outbound transit; Alfonso's status is unclear — it is on Iran's PGSA non-compliance blacklist. UKMTO's October tally is now 24 warnings plus 3 advisories.
items.title: Tuesday saw four Hormuz ship attacks, not two; vessels identified, UKMTO Oct tally hits 24

items.summary: Twelve senators (Republicans McConnell, Tillis, Collins, Armstrong, Murkowski, Cornyn; Democrats Blumenthal, Shaheen, Durbin, Whitehouse, Reed, Coons) wrote to Trump on Oct 13 urging him to rescind OFAC General License No. 135, which temporarily eased sanctions to let Russian diesel into global markets. They called the deal a "gift to our adversary," arguing Kremlin revenue would finance Russia's war and advance security cooperation with China, Iran and North Korea, endanger servicemembers in Operation Epic Fury, and offer negligible fuel-price relief despite the Iran war's pressure on diesel. They want the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 enforced instead. A separate Sunday statement by seven senators said the deal runs counter to the 2022 Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act. Trump defended the deal Tuesday en route to Alaska, calling it "a deal for the world." Catch-up item: published before this run's last_check but missed by earlier checks.
items.title: Bipartisan senators urge Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal tied to Iran-war fuel prices

items.summary: The IRGC Navy said via IRNA on Saturday that two oil tankers carrying about two million barrels of crude each caught fire after striking naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz on a route Tehran had not authorized; one vessel was left immobilized. Iranian state media said the ships had switched off positioning and radar systems. There was no independent confirmation of the reports.
items.title: IRGC Navy claims two oil tankers hit naval mines in Hormuz

items.summary: Iran's navy accused US forces of firing two light projectiles at a 35mm anti-aircraft cannon at the Konarak naval base on Iran's southeastern coast around 1 a.m. local Monday, wounding two personnel. If confirmed, it would be the first US strike on Iranian soil since Sept 1. A US official told CNN the Iranian claim was inaccurate. Separately, the IRGC claimed air defenses destroyed the 54th US MQ-9 drone over the strait Monday night; a US official dismissed the claim.
items.title: Iran says US struck Konarak naval base, wounding 2; US disputes the claim

items.summary: The IRGC Navy said two more 'non-compliant' oil tankers were set ablaze after hitting mines it laid on an unauthorized passage south of the strait, warning that 'if the US mischief continues, oil companies will have to pay a heavier price'; Iranian state TV reported a third tanker exploded after hitting a mine, carrying over two million barrels of crude. IRGC Maj. Gen. Mostafa Izadi said Iran's control of the strait will continue 'for as long as the Islamic Republic of Iran decides,' IRGC spokesman Mojabi threatened undersea internet cables and 'new weapons,' and FM spokesman Baghaei vowed Tehran would answer any US strike 'in equal measure, if not more forcefully.' All claims are Iranian-state-only, with no independent verification.
items.title: IRGC claims two more tankers ablaze after mine hits; threatens oil firms and undersea cables

items.summary: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told Fox News Digital the agency cannot declare the strait safe: its information is that the approved 1968 traffic-separation route still has mines, and third-party verification is impossible while the conflict continues. He said the strait is 'not open for business in the way that it was before the conflict started' and that Iran's own unauthorized corridor inside its territorial waters was never put through IMO approval.
items.title: IMO chief: Hormuz traffic-separation route still has mines; cannot guarantee safety

items.summary: FM Abbas Araqchi said Iran's mid-September proposal — reopen the strait within six days, talks resume the next day — remains on the table while Tehran reviews the US response; conditions include lifting the US port blockade, ending oil-export sanctions, and ending hostilities on all fronts. SNSC chief Rezaei said via IRNA/Reuters that Washington has accepted some of Tehran's seven conditions but issues remain. Baghaei said quick results are unrealistic, the UAE's Anwar Gargash said no unilateral Iranian navigation arrangements 'can be trusted,' and Araqchi said Tehran has received no response from Saudi Arabia or the Houthis to its peace-broker offer.
items.title: Iran says Hormuz reopening offer still on table if US accepts its conditions

items.summary: Brent touched a five-month high of $111.99 on Tuesday, settling at $108.79, and traded near $109.64 on Wednesday on Middle East supply fears (Reuters). Ship-tracker Kpler counted at least 18 vessel attacks in the fortnight to Oct 20, and LSEG analysts said Iran is targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Gulf crude flows recovered to about 80% of prewar levels though refined-product shipments remain constrained; Iran's First VP Aref said Tehran has 'no choice' but to assert control over Hormuz.
items.title: Brent hits ~$110, a five-month high, as Hormuz attacks mount

items.event_time_ist: Oct 17, 2026 (CBS News town hall, aired Saturday evening)
items.summary: Joey Amor, husband of Master Sgt. Nicole Amor — one of six Army reservists killed in Iran's March 1 drone strike on Port Shuaiba, Kuwait, the deadliest attack on US forces in the war — confronted VP JD Vance at a CBS News town hall over 'fundamental failures': thin fortifications, no counter-drone capacity, troops not rebased farther from Iran, and an ignored request for more medical support. Vance said it was 'literally the first time' he had heard the concerns and pledged to examine them.
items.title: Widower of soldier killed in March Kuwait strike presses Vance on failures
